sentences.text: Revenue rose from $129,025.0m in FY2017 [F1] to $303,154.0m in FY2026 [F10], a 10.0% compound rate [F203].
Growth stepped up in FY2021 and FY2022, at 17.5% [D189] and 15.8% [D238], then slowed to 6.8% in FY2023 [D287].
The filing ties FY2021 to comparable sales up 16% [P56] and FY2022 to comparable sales up 14% [P42], with inflation lifting sales in both years [P42][P56].
Net income compounded faster, at 14.7% [F205] against revenue's 10.0% [F203], and rose 25.1% in FY2021 [D191].
In FY2026, Net Sales contributed 9.9pp of 10.1% growth [D535][D434], and warehouse ancillary and other businesses was the largest driver at 3.7pp [D601].
The filing cites comparable sales up 8% and 25 new warehouses [P14], and says ancillary sales grew faster than core merchandise [P12], where ancillary growth was 19.9% [D600].
Operating income grew 12.5% [D435] against 10.1% revenue growth [D434], an incremental margin of 4.7% [D457] versus 9.6% in FY2024 [D359].
Diluted EPS compounded at 14.6% [F207], just below net income's 14.7% [F205], as diluted shares rose from 440.9m [X91] to 444.4m [X100].
FY2023 had an extra week of sales [P32] and FY2024 one fewer [P27], so their 6.8% [D287] and 5.0% [D336] growth rates are not like-for-like.
Operating margin was 3.9% in FY2026 [F32], the window high [D691] and above the 3.4% median [D692] and 3.1% low [D690].
Against retail peers it ranks at the 17th percentile [D709], versus a 5.0% peer median [D710].
The 0.3pp gain in FY2024 [D349], the window's largest, came with cost of revenue adding 0.4pp [D361]; gross margin rose 35 basis points, helped by absent charter-shipping charges [P24].
In FY2022 cost of revenue cut margin 0.7pp [D263] and SG&A added 0.7pp [D264]; the filing ties the gross margin fall to a 19 basis point LIFO charge [P40] and SG&A gains to sales leverage [P38].
Net margin of 3.0% [F52] trails operating margin of 3.9% [F32] after a 24.7% effective tax rate [D420].
Operating cash flow of $15,817.0m [F82] was 1.71x net income [D421], and free cash flow was 1.02x [D422] against a 0.99x window median [D701].
The filing ties the 18.6% operating cash rise [D439] to higher operating income and lower inventory investment from faster turns [P6].
Capex was 2.41x D&A [D423], up from 1.83x in FY2017 [D11].

FY2022 was the weakest year, with free cash flow at 0.60x net income [D226]; that year's operating-cash passage is cut off before naming a cause [P35], so the link to inventory growth of 26.0% [D260] is unconfirmed by the filing.
Net cash was $15,139.0m [D427], or 5.0% of revenue [D428], at FY2026.
That ranks at the 100th percentile among six retail peers [D715], against a -4.4% peer median [D716].

Long-term debt fell from $6,573.0m in FY2017 [F183] to $3,914.0m [F192], but total debt rose 6.5% in FY2026 [D454] as the current portion reached $2,248.0m [X160]; the cited passages do not explain that move.
Buybacks of $848.0m [X110] and dividends of $2,458.0m [X120] took 35.2% of free cash flow [D430], and diluted shares fell 0.1% [D452].
The net cash and payout leave room to absorb a working-capital reversal [D427][D430], though the pack gives no forward buyback guidance.
Dividends and buybacks reached 146.9% of FY2024 free cash flow [D332], with dividends of $9,041.0m [X118], and cash and investments fell 26.8% [D355]; the cited passages do not explain the payment.
Receivables grew 23.6% [D455], well ahead of 10.1% revenue growth [D434], to $3,959.0m [X190]; the cited passages do not explain the rise.
The balance is small, with 5 days sales outstanding [D431] against 4 in FY2025 [D382], so the concern is direction more than size.
FY2026 margin includes $184 of IEEPA tariff refunds [P15], which the filing says added three basis points to gross margin net of member price cuts [P12].
Most refunds are being reinvested in member value [P15], so FY2026 margin is not a clean base for the next year.
In the FY2027 10-K, operating margin holding at or above 3.9% [F32] confirms the trend; a fall toward the 3.4% median [D692] reverses it.
In the FY2027 10-K, free cash flow to net income above 1.02x [D422] confirms conversion; a drop toward the 0.99x median [D701] signals fading working-capital support.
In the FY2027 10-K, inventory days at or below 27 [D432] keep the working-capital benefit; a rise toward FY2022's 33 days [D236] reverses it.
